annotations.title: Look up the words a law defines

description: What a word means in a Japanese law that defines it. The words a law defines for itself (定義語): inside that law, and only as far as each definition reaches, the word means what the statute says, not what it means in everyday speech or in another law. For each, the statute's own words (statuteJa), its reading, its English and whose that is (englishWhose), a plain explanation by japanlaw.org (explanation, in lang), where it is defined (definedAt, url) and how far it reaches (scope, scopeLabel). With address — {"law": "labor-standards-act", "address": "art-36"} — the definitions that apply in that provision, because its text uses the word, and japanlaw.org's explanations of the words of Japanese law it uses (concepts: 施行, 政令, 附則…). Call it before explaining what a provision means. term narrows the answer to one word, in Japanese, its reading or its English. A law with many terms stops at one; continued.cursor, passed back as cursor with the same arguments, goes on. The text in force only.

address.description: A provision: the definitions that apply in it, and the legal vocabulary it uses. Unset lists every term the law defines. Written as for get_provision: 第三十六条, Article 36(2) or art-36/par-2.

cursor.description: Go on from here: the cursor an earlier answer's continued gave, with the same law, address and term.

lang.description: The language of the pages every url opens, and of the card get_provision is drawn as: "en" (default) or "ja". The text returned always holds both languages.

law.description: The law: its Japanese title (労働基準法), English title (Labor Standards Act), short name (労基法), slug (labor-standards-act) or e-Gov law ID (322AC0000000049).

term.description: One word to look up: the term (労働者), its reading (ろうどうしゃ) or its English (worker).

name: get_definitions
